newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-NSW CRUSH SOUTH AUSTRALIA BY AN INNINGS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NSW CRUSH SOUTH AUSTRALIA BY AN INNINGS.

text.p: All-rounder Brad McNamara ended with figures of five for 19 as New South Wales crushed South Australia by an innings and 169 runs in their Sheffield Shield match at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Sunday.
Despite a late start to the final day because of heavy rain, New South Wales only needed 55 minutes to finish off the last four South Australian batsmen.
After resuming on 68 for six, South Australia capitulated to be all out for 117 to give New South Wales a temporary share of the Shield leadership alongside Queensland and Western Australia.
Former Australian all-rounder Shane Lee took two wickets in the short remaining session, with Greg Matthews taking one and McNamara his fifth of the innings.
Matthews made 109 not out on Saturday and declared the NSW first innings at 440 for six for a lead of 286.

It was the third outright win for NSW this season, but they have played two more games than Queensland and one more than Western Australia, who look to be in control against Tasmania in Hobart with one day remaining.
Western Australian captain Tom Moody was the main destroyer for his side, taking seven for 41, his second-best career bowling performance.
Tasmania were shot out for 175 in their second innings and at the close of play on the third day, Western Australia had reached 27 for no wicket, needing to score a further 151 for outright victory.
Earlier on Sunday, Tasmania took first innings points by dismissing the Warriors for 312, just short of their first innings tally of 314.
But the home side's batting crumbled before Moody's medium pace bowling, opener Jamie Cox providing most resistance with 51.
